<system-reminder>
The tools listed below are available in this environment, but their schemas may be omitted from the current tool list to save context.
Load a listed tool with ToolSearch: pass query "select:<name>[,<name>...]" with the exact names listed below, or pass keywords (e.g. "linear issue") to search tool names and descriptions and auto-load the best matches.
Prefer the exact names below when you know them; use a keyword query to discover a tool by capability. Do not call an omitted tool directly (it fails with InputValidationError); if a tool is neither currently available, listed below, nor found by keyword, it is unavailable this session.

IMPORTANT: When the task matches a listed tool, load and use it rather than routing around it using Execute. Examples: FetchUrl instead of `curl/wget/gh pr view`, WebSearch instead of Execute `gh search` or scraping search engines, the corresponding MCP tool instead of Execute `curl` against an MCP endpoint.

</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Connector tools let you act on the user's connected external apps (for example GitHub, Linear, Jira) through the ConnectorSearch tool. When connectivity is known, connected tools are listed in a separate reminder, so no discovery call is needed for listed tools.

Connectors usage rules:
- An enabled MCP server or a skill dedicated to that same service takes priority; use connectors only when neither covers the need. A generic browser, scraping, or shell fallback does not count as covering a service.
- When a connected connector tool matches what the user needs from an external app, call it via ConnectorSearch (action "call_tool") instead of the shell or web search.
- The connectivity reminder lists only connected apps, so an app missing from it may still be offered by the organization and merely unconnected. Never conclude that no connector exists for an app without checking, and never tell the user an app is unavailable on that basis.
- For an app that is not listed as connected, and that the user needs data or actions from (including a link they pasted): use its MCP server tools if any; otherwise call ConnectorSearch "list_tools" (without authenticatedOnly) to check whether the organization offers it, then "call_tool". If the result asks for authentication, share the returned connect link with the user and retry after they connect. Fall back to a browser, scraping, or the shell only after that check shows the app is not offered.
- Refer to the brokering platform as "Connectors" or by the specific app's name (for example GitHub); share connect links as-is without drawing attention to the underlying provider.
- A connected app is not permission to act on the user's behalf. Reads are fine, and when the user asks for a write (posting a Slack or Teams message, sending an email, commenting, approving or landing a pull request, changing an issue), carry it out through the connector and send only what they asked for. Never write on your own initiative: for a write the user did not request, ask for explicit permission first and then send only what they approved.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Available skills (invoke by exact name when its description matches the request):
agent-browser: Automates browsers and Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, etc.) for testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate, interact with, test, or extract data from any website or Electron desktop app. Prefer dedicated tools for simple searches, documentation lookups, or app data when they cover the task.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.
detect-overlapping-workstreams: Check whether a Software Factory workstream duplicates one that already exists in the org - the same goal, the same repositories, or the same intake sources - and warn the user before the redundant work starts. Use when creating a workstream, or when asked whether a goal is already covered by an existing one.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review the complete intended change for reuse, quality, compatibility provenance, and efficiency, then fix verified issues.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content
pdf-document: Produce polished PDF documents (reports, invoices, resumes, letters, flyers, certificates, any "export to PDF" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PDF or a printable document.
powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.
excel: Produce polished Excel spreadsheets (reports, budgets, data exports, any "export to Excel" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for an Excel file, a spreadsheet, or an .xlsx deliverable.
word-document: Produce polished Word documents (reports, letters, proposals, printable docs, any .docx deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a Word document or a .docx file.
install-qa: Use when the user wants to set up automated QA testing for a project. Analyzes the codebase, runs a guided questionnaire, and generates a modular QA skill with per-app sub-skills, CI integration (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI), and a standardized report template.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini) when public model endpoints are available, and a documented single-family BYOK degradation in airgap mode. A protected line-anchor floor runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; vendor and ecosystem prior-art enrichments run only when public network access is allowed. A conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, DASHBOARD.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
incident: RCA runbook for alerts. Given an alert link (or prompted to provide one), identifies the alert type, verifies tooling/auth, and walks through root cause analysis using deep research. Persists learnings to incident-guidelines for future reuse.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.
wiki-video-gen: Generate Factory-branded HyperFrames video overviews for repository wikis. Use when wiki generation reaches Phase 3.6, or when the user asks for a narrated repository overview video.
install-wiki: Install a CI action that automatically refreshes the Factory Wiki on each push to the default branch. Use when the user wants to set up automated wiki generation, install wiki CI, or configure wiki refresh.
browse-wiki: Search and read wiki documentation for a repository
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Available subagents for the Task tool are listed below. The Task tool relies on this system reminder for valid subagent_type names.

When a user task matches an available subagent, prefer launching it via the Task tool over doing the work yourself.


Built-in subagent types:
- worker: General-purpose read/write worker for bounded implementation, research, analysis, and validation. (default complexity: medium)
- explorer: Use for specific, well-scoped codebase questions. Read-only. (default complexity: light)
</system-reminder>
